## Exact change and quality budget

Each private function is a literal copy of the original SSR function, changing
only its name, the binary-refinement loop bound to4/3/2, and all its depth/color
fetches to explicit base-level syntax. Outer loop, adaptive increment
max(SSR_STEP_SIZE*abs(diffZ)*invR,1.0), reflected direction, offscreen exit,
epsilon/cutoffs, oldPos/curPos hit bracket, vignette/fresnel, final depth guard
and miss result are retained. Original native function and sampling syntax
remain intact. No light/shadow budgets change.

Mode2 computes one length(viewPos) from the originating reconstructed
camera/view-space position in Minecraft blocks. Near clamps to0; far clamps to
at least near+1. At/below near selects4, strictly between near/far selects3,
at/beyond far selects2. It is not feet length, raw depth, axial z, world origin,
reflected hit distance or time-varying noise. Integer transitions are stable for
a fixed camera but can create moving rings; this is deliberately not advertised
as a smooth quality transition. Root must inspect crossings and stop promotion
if quality fails. No second full SSR path or complete-path blend executes.

Only an eligible first hit inside the existing refinement cutoff saves samples:
at most one depth refinement fetch in the middle zone, two in the far zone.
Outer march coverage and first-hit bracket stay intact, but final refined UV,
hit acceptance, thin geometry and reflected color can change. Many pixels miss
or skip refinement already, so full-frame savings may be negligible. Near/full4
uses new fetch syntax and cannot be called exact pixel parity until mode1 versus
original is compared on the driver. All three literal copies enlarge source;
inlining, register allocation and instruction-cache effects can offset savings.
Mode1 allows the compiler to discard unused2/3 copies, so its code shape is not
a complete control for every mode2 compiler effect.

Actual binaries show that `MultiDrawBatch` moved from `gl/device` to

The new redirect selects each version's exact `DefaultChunkRenderer.render`
descriptor and its sole `MultiDrawBatch.draw(DrawContext)` invocation. It reads
`GLDrawBatch`'s private arrays through a pinned accessor and emits a private
submission copy on the same pass. Its native cached pointers, counts, bases,
size, maximum count and filled state never change. Unsupported passes, shadow
rendering, unexpected batch/context types or failed admission call native draw.

The actual OpenGL `GlRenderPass.multiDrawIndexed` calls
`GlCommandEncoder.executeDraws`, which synchronously calls
`nglMultiDrawElementsBaseVertex` before returning. Scoped `MemoryStack` storage
therefore survives through CPU pointer consumption. The candidate caps a batch
at 1,024 commands and declines copying if the current stack lacks space. A driver
submission failure propagates; it never retries a possibly submitted draw.

## Geometry and identity proof

Only adjacent commands with zero index pointers and contiguous vertex ranges
may merge. Counts must be positive multiples of six, bases must be nonnegative,
and final vertex addresses must fit signed integers. Any invalid tail refuses
the whole batch before destination writes. Every merged count is at most the
native cached batch's original maximum; Sodium has already ensured shared-index
capacity for that maximum. This port does not reuse or change the old growth
formula. Native index generation is `0,1,2,2,3,0` for each consecutive four
vertices, so flattening adjacent quad ranges preserves the exact triangle and
provoking-vertex order.

Both pinned Iris transformers set `_draw_id = a_LightAndData[3]`; chunk
translation and fading use that vertex attribute. The candidate preserves the
vertex stream, base-adjusted indices, current region, pipeline and uniforms.
Existing full original MakeUp 9.5g/native100 and Sildur certificates are reused
for unchanged pack input. Actual transformed shader capture is still required:
old source certificates and new static transformer inspection are not a driver
consumption or quality pass on these versions.

## Target arithmetic and honest upper bounds

For throughput multiplier `S=1.5`, target total duration is `T0/S`. If an
independent critical-path effect is fraction `p` and sped up `k` times, the
optimistic retained duration is `1-p+p/k`; achievable multiplier is its inverse.
This assumes additive cost, unchanged remaining work, zero transition/branch/
reconstruction overhead, and no CPU/presentation bottleneck migration. It is a
conditional upper bound, not a model fit to the current pass data.

| Hypothetical effect speedup | Minimum affected total-frame share to reach 1.5× |
| --- | ---: |
| Complete removal | 33.333% |
| 4× | 44.444% |
| 3× | 50.000% |
| 2× | 66.667% |

A completely removable 20% share can produce at most 1.25× throughput under these
assumptions. For distant work only, use `p = effect share × distant-work share`;
pixel fraction is not a cost fraction. Distance LOD that halves an effect whose
total-frame share is 20% saves at most 10% duration before overhead, even if every
pixel is eligible. No calibrated current effect share is established here.

If 10% faster were later independently accepted, 1.10× throughput corresponds
to 9.091% lower duration; reaching 1.50× would still require 26.667% less duration
than that improved candidate. If “10%” instead means GPU-time reduction, it is
11.111% GPU-interval throughput uplift and says nothing by itself about total FPS.

# Explicit adapter target and pass layout

2026-10-05. The dependency-free
[`layout`](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/lod/adapter/layout/AdapterLayout.java)
API validates immutable, adapter-supplied image allocations, quantity views,
reads, simultaneous draw groups and full-target viewports. It complements the
[work adapter contract](LOD_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md) and
[spatial pipeline](SPATIAL_LOD_PIPELINE.md). It contains no pack names, attachment
indices, GLSL parser, rewriting, source discovery or automatic source certificate.
An accepted declaration proves structural consistency of that declaration only.

The motivating diagnostic failure resized target 11 while a later upstream draw
still bound targets 11 and 12 at different dimensions. A producer-only target
check would miss this conflict. Adapters must declare **every reachable draw
group**, including preserved upstream groups. The validator compares every
attachment to the first, including a third or later attachment; it never stops
after one matching pair.

| Declaration | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Dimensions` | Positive integer level-zero image or viewport dimensions. |
| `TargetSize.Absolute` | Fixed allocation dimensions. |
| `TargetSize.Relative` | Independent rational width/height scales of the rendered surface, each with explicit FLOOR or CEIL. |
| `TargetDeclaration` | Namespaced logical image identity, size, reviewed format and one or more quantity views. |
| `Quantity` | Namespaced basis/schema key, storage role, required channels and, for bounded float integers, an explicit maximum magnitude. |
| `PassDeclaration.Read` | Explicit image identity and numeric/unfiltered fetch declaration. |
| `PassDeclaration.DrawGroup` | Attachments simultaneously drawn with one viewport. Separate groups may use different dimensions. |
| `AdapterLayout` | Immutable targets and ordered pass declarations. Duplicate target/pass identities are schema errors. |
| `LayoutValidation` | Immutable resolved target dimensions and located failures; `valid()` means no structural failure. |

Sizes use actual rendered surface dimensions, not display size. Positive int
scale terms multiply in long; even maximum int terms plus the CEIL adjustment
fit long. Resolution rejects zero after FLOOR and any result above
`Integer.MAX_VALUE`, rather than truncating or wrapping. At 1709 × 961,
CEIL half/quarter allocations are 855 × 481 and 428 × 241. This matches the
spatial kernel's allocation formula; incomplete receiver tiles still require
the adapter's full fallback. A declaration can never prove that shader mapping.

Every group must have equal attachment dimensions and a viewport equal to those
dimensions. Smaller viewports fail `VIEWPORT_UNDERSIZED`; larger ones fail
`VIEWPORT_OVERSIZED`. A viewport smaller on one axis and larger on another reports
both. Partial draws, atlas region offsets and mip/subresource layouts are outside
this initial contract. Do not suppress this full-target check to authorize them.
Unknown read/write identities and failed allocation formulas invalidate the
layout; remaining independent checks still run.

Direct read/write overlap is rejected under `FeedbackPolicy.UNSUPPORTED`.
`DISTINCT_IMAGES_EXTERNALLY_VERIFIED` declares that the same logical identity
uses **physically distinct** read/write images, for example reviewed ping-pong.
It never authorizes sampling the same image being drawn. The adapter/runtime
owner must establish those distinct images; the validator cannot inspect GL
bindings, aliasing, pass completion or renderer flip/clear behavior.

## Storage and exact certificates

Each quantity view declares its own channel requirement; views can occupy
different texels of one allocation. Their channel counts are not summed. Packing,
locations, lifetimes, units and decode remain explicit adapter obligations.
Known formats are deliberately reviewed enum entries; unsupported formats need
an explicit API extension and checks, rather than inference from shader text.

- `GENERAL` checks channel capacity; `LINEAR_QUANTITY` also requires float storage.
  Neither validates that a shader expression is a linear basis.
- `EXACT_SIGNED_INT32_METADATA` / `EXACT_UNSIGNED_INT32_METADATA` require matching
  32-bit integer storage and signed/unsigned integer `texelFetch` declarations.
  RGBA16I, floating point and signed/unsigned reinterpretations fail.
- `BINARY32_MINIMUM_DISTANCE` requires 32-bit float storage and
  `Fetch.FLOAT_TEXEL_FETCH`. Half-float or filtered reads cannot certify an exact
  conservative minimum. Raw float bits stored in integer metadata instead use
  the exact integer role; preservation via `floatBitsToInt` / `intBitsToFloat`
  remains source/driver proof.
- `EXACT_BINARY32_BOUNDED_INTEGER_METADATA` requires an explicit maximum integer
  magnitude in **[1, 16777216]**, 32-bit float storage and
  `Fetch.FLOAT_TEXEL_FETCH`. Every integer in that signed magnitude interval is
  representable in binary32. 16777217 is not; it rounds to 16777216. Ordinary
  float storage does not automatically grant this metadata role. Fractional,
  out-of-domain, stale or misdecoded shader values are not inspected by Java.

`FLOAT_OR_NORMALIZED` declares ordinary float/normalized reads; it cannot read
integer textures or satisfy exact float metadata/distance fetch requirements.
The integer fetch variants declare unfiltered integer addressing. Actual shader
instructions and runtime texture/sampler state must separately match declarations.

Distance is Euclidean camera-relative view space in Minecraft blocks. Below

hit displacement from zero to0.25 depth-texture texel. The transition is continuous
in error tolerance; discrete iteration changes still require motion QA.
Footprint is calculated explicitly from the projected ray step and effective
view resolution/TAAU scale, without derivatives or implicit LOD sampling.

At least one original refinement update executes before stopping. Every possible
remaining original position must fit inside the same valid fetched depth texel
with conservative boundary margins. Thus its sampled hand/sky/terrain depth and
original final-depth eligibility are preserved. In addition, the entire remaining
z envelope must lie uniformly inside/outside the original depth-hit predicate
with a margin, projected UV displacement must be<=0.25texel, and remaining screen
depth uncertainty<=1/16 original depth tolerance. Screen depth is nonlinear:
the actual pinned Photon project() structure supplies a division-free homogeneous
endpoint bound, with an explicit float32 error envelope. Homogeneous W must have
no pole, and conservative Euclidean view displacement must stay within0.049block,
reserving1mm toward a0.05block cap. Near/far view displacement is never inferred
from NDC error alone.
This bound does not prove perceptual parity of reprojected color or fog.

A secondary cache reuses only the immediately preceding valid integer texel's

reused. Original ray arithmetic and every coarse hit test remain. First refinement
can reuse its just-found coarse depth. Thin edges, different texels and failed

## R2 guard cost revision and numerical invariants

Implemented only review items1–3 in the isolated managed
`/Users/pippo/.codex/worktrees/reflection-guard-cost/shaderlod` worktree based
24f4d3d. Main archives/runtime/combined pins are unchanged. Coarse depth cache
(item4), all original fetch positions/weights, sampler/projection selection,
0.25texel threshold,1/16depth tolerance and policy interface are unchanged.
No new options, consumer uniforms, passes or target slots are introduced.

Uniform policy must activate before radial length is computed. The refinement
stop guard accepts remaining2..7 only. Remaining1 or>7 runs every original cached
update; larger total budgets may become eligible later when their remaining count
falls to<=7, so this is a per-attempt conservative subset, not a whole-ray count
change. Extent uses the exact float32 binary fraction
`1 − (1 << (7−remaining))/128`; this removes two exp2 expression evaluations and
accuracy assumptions. Necessary pixel/span-z limits execute before texel envelope
or inverse-space work. There is still no late texture fetch whose result is thrown
away. Early stop saves no additional depth fetches over exact cached continuation;
it saves only original cached refinement updates/key/hit tests. Cache and stopping
cost/benefit must remain separate in measurements.

`shaderlod_reflection_view_bound` replaces three endpoint projections/three vec3
divides with one homogeneous center/change calculation, beginning with scalar z/W.
Its z error is a necessary cheap rejection before x/y work. It uses the actual
pinned global project helper (global SHA256
6235933d0045282ba9d7822d55a40aaff6b76ac862c550e33f9b8a4229d63c3d).
The manifest and executable fixture pin both this member and exact helper text;
the existing builder's full original ZIP SHA authenticates the same source, so
no builder changes were needed.

For H=project(M,2pos−1), dH=diag(M)*(2step*extent).xyzz, the exact endpoint change
is ±(dH.xyz*H.w−H.xyz*dH.w)/(H.w*(H.w±dH.w)). Without rounding, absolute W has
minimum |H.w|−|dH.w| along the segment. The guard adds a homogeneous difference
error envelope E, reduces minimum W by E.w, and inflates the numerator by
`E.xyz*|H.w| + |H.xyz|*E.w`, expression cancellation error and two projected
divisions' rounding bounds. No actual divisions are computed in the guard.
Finite numerator/denominator squares and conservative outward factors reject
Inf<=Inf, NaN and denominator poles.

The E envelope is1e−6 times positive matrix/coordinate/offset/current/change terms,
plus1e−30. For round-to-nearest float32 u=2^-24, at most7successive future position
adds have gamma7=7u/(1−7u)<4.18e−7. The chosen positive scale covers that accumulated
position error, both NDC conversions, project/change multiplication/addition and
FMA/non-FMA differences; it uses matrix magnitudes rather than only cancellation-
small H. Finite matrix entries/offsets<=1e6 and pos/step components<=4 bound all
products/squares below overflow. W and its error-reduced minimum must exceed1e−6.
Numerator inflation1.00001, denominator deflation0.99999 and a second squared-cap
deflation cover rounding in the positive bound expressions. The1mm final world
reserve is retained. The explicit tiny error floor dominates float32 underflow
error in bounded products; tiny squared numerators cannot bypass a pole rejection.
No same-z shortcut or unverified derivative shortcut was added.

This conservative envelope can reject most far-depth attempts, so fewer source
divides does not imply a GPU or total-frame improvement. Additional safety ALU,
cache branches/registers and footprint eligibility distribution remain risks.
First r2 acceptance needs a fresh source-qualified driver/reload/readback smoke;
then matched repeated original/off/on GPU and total-frame comparisons plus a
cache-only attribution control and reflection/fog/motion checks. Archive pins in
queued r1 and combined runs must never be silently replaced with this revision.

## Entry points, counters and units

Trace is private/default OFF. The selected code requires
`SHADERLOD_WORK_TRACE`, Overworld `PROGRAM_DEFERRED1`, and absence of
`ATMOSPHERE_TRANSMITTANCE_LUT`. Entry is
`shaders/world0/deferred1.fsh` → `program/d1_clouds.fsh` → `draw_clouds` →
`draw_cumulus_clouds`. Original/global-OFF fallback uses Photon cumulus; adapted
execution uses `shaderlod_volume_draw_cumulus` in the
[diagnostic adapter copy](../shaderpacks/photon-shared-work-trace/shaders/include/shaderlod/photon_volume_trace_adapter.glsl).

The common trace is initialized once per fragment. Increments occur at reached
operations, including early density returns; they do not derive work from the
requested cap, density strength, final radiance or history.

| Counter | Exact unit |
| --- | --- |
| Primary iterations | Reached primary loop body after the transmittance-break check, before adapted partial-cell rejection |
| Density evaluations | Cumulus density function entries, both primary and secondary, including shell/coverage/altitude early zero returns |
| Secondary visits | Reached optical-depth loop bodies, lighting and sky; excludes the eight-iteration scattering approximation |
| Texture evaluations | Reached texture-value calls in cumulus density/local coverage: local coverage map, both Worley fields, or two procedural coverage reads |

Texture counts exclude `textureSize`, depth/dither samples, other cloud layers,
crepuscular rays, atmosphere and post-lighting work. They are source-level
texture evaluations, not hardware fetches or instruction counts. The secondary
unit is deliberately narrower than all secondary arithmetic.

Page 1 records the original primary budget and the actual selected draw body's
continuous target. `requested_work` means the target supplied to that draw,
including existing footprint/protection restoration; it does not expose the
unprotected policy ratio or preflight request. Original uses N/N/N; adapted
uses N/target/target. Coverage-zero exits occur before upstream computes N and
retain initialized zero budgets, while the known selected path is recorded.
Path 0 means no cumulus draw; 1 means original/fallback; 2 means adapted; 3 is
reserved and unused. Reason 0 is the only emitted reason: individual wrapper
fallback causes are not classified. This boundary is explicit in the metadata.

## Work duplicated or performed without benefit

**Two complete classifications per tile.** Prepass lines 302–314 call shared
produce in quantity lane and shared prepare again in certificate lane. Shared
prepare (`spatial_pipeline.glsl:76–108`) calls surface for all four members before
the classifier can reject one; both lanes together make eight surface calls.
Successful eligible surfaces each fetch depth1, gbuffer1 and overlay3, project,
decode normal/lightmap and call material_from: **24 texture fetches/tile** just
for these duplicate preparations. Each successful classifier checks four member
records, one cell and six member pairs; the duplicated path checks eight records,
two cells and twelve pairs. It initializes arrays of length16 in each lane even
for side2; compiler elimination/unrolling/register pressure is unmeasured.

Demand is tested **after** preparation and region eligibility
(`spatial_pipeline.glsl:115–121`). FULL/global OFF/INHERIT/invalid policy,
availability0, wet environment and legal unity endpoints can therefore incur
preparation with zero representative lighting. Surface early returns reduce
individual fetches for sky/masked/hand members, but do not skip the four callbacks.
Current FULL still performs the two preparations whenever cache contract passes.

**The current distance policy has a large no-demand zone.** With medium retention1
and far0.25, the quarter tier weight is zero up to the far transition start,
96 − 8/2 = 92 blocks. The classification near guard is only 32 − 8/2 = 28 blocks.
Regions between 28 and 92 can pass geometry, pay the whole duplicate classification
and then discover no quarter work. Near32 is not the sharing start for these
actual ratios. Policy validity and legal endpoint checks, not a hard-coded
distance, must govern any earlier skip.

**Repeated AO union.** Adapter evaluate_linear calls the AO union guard every
time (`photon_spatial_adapter.glsl:89–97`). In an ordinary interior tile at
taau_render_scale = 1 the union covers 3 × 3 taps, each reading ambient6 and depth14:
18 fetches before original evaluation. The evaluation then repeats the original
four ambient/four depth taps, plus depth1/gbuffer1 and overlay3: 11 additional
explicit fetches, before variable shadow/noise work. This is 29 fetches per basis
callback plus original variable lighting work; not a GPU instruction count.

For one successful pure-quarter tile, preparations 24 + basis 29 + consumer cache 8
= **61 explicit fetch calls** in those paths alone, excluding both main preludes,
variable shadows/noise and recipient material/fog. Original selected AO evaluation
has 32 explicit AO/depth taps across the four recipients, but this is not a full
original-frame fetch budget. These different totals must not be compared as total
memory traffic or a time ratio.

For one successful full/quarter transition tile with four full bases, the same
AO union runs five times: 90 guard fetches, and selected lighting evaluates five
times versus original four. This is a real structural +25% evaluation count for
that selected operation in that case. Geometry/current-snapshot and AO
certification could potentially authorize guard reuse, but their current contract
does not expose an explicit reusable AO success certificate. Do not remove the
guard on an assumption or relax its threshold to create eligibility.

**Full fallback and sky staging.** The consumer retains original G-buffer decode,
material evaluation and unconditional atmosphere/cloud prelude; it adds initial
plan/material/environment/resolve checks before original fallback AO/shadows/
diffuse. The producer also contains the original atmosphere/cloud prelude before
any divergence (`shaderlod_spatial_prepass.fsh:224–255`). It evaluates original
sky at full resolution and the consumer replaces its original sky body with a
completed0 fetch. The original sky body itself is moved, not evaluated twice.
The prelude occurs in both source programs, with terrain cloud composition still
full resolution. Driver/compiler liveness and actual execution cost are unknown;
do not claim two full atmosphere evaluations at every pixel from source alone.
Moving implicit sampling inside a tile/depth branch previously failed source
review. Any staging change must preserve derivative scope and parity.

Invalid/masked/nonplanar/lightmap-varying/normal-varying tiles, hand/sky, overlays,

## The pinned algorithm is already a vertex-plane test

`net.irisshaders.iris.shadows.frustum.advanced.AdvancedShadowCullingFrustum`
does **not** allocate/evaluate eight corner vectors per AABB. Its constructor
builds up to thirteen planes, including light-extruded edge planes, with JOML
vectors. Per-box `checkCornerVisibility(FFFFFF)I` instead chooses positive and
negative vertices using coefficient signs and evaluates two dot expressions
per plane. Constructor vector allocation should not be confused with this
hot per-box path.

The relevant pinned methods and bytecode offsets:

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `checkCornerVisibility`, offsets 24–73 | Positive vertex: select min coordinate if coefficient `<0`, otherwise max |
| Same, 75–114 / 205–238 | Evaluate positive dot; reject unless result `>= -plane[3]` |
| Same, 115–198 / 239–322 | Evaluate negative dot and update fully-inside flag, for every surviving plane |
| Same, 335–345 | Return 1 if fully inside, 2 if intersecting; outside returned 0 earlier |
| `testAab`, 0–53 | Preserve Sodium distance box rejection, call tri-state check, use only `>0` |
| `isVisible(DDDDDD)`, 0–74 | Subtract camera in double, cast each endpoint to float, then classify |
| `fastAabbTest` | Distance check plus tri-state result, potentially consumed as a classification |

FMA support is selected from HotSpot's `UseFMA` flag. Positive dot order is
`fma(px,x, fma(py,y, pz*z))`; negative dot uses
`fma(px,x, fma(py,y, fma(pz,z,pw)))`. In the fallback, `safeFMA(a,b,c)` is
separate float multiplication then float addition. Preserve that rounding
order; algebraic equivalence over real numbers is insufficient at the plane
boundary.

## Rank 1: boolean-only positive-vertex test for Sodium

Sodium's hot boolean entry point does not need the fully-inside classification.
Keep the existing box-culler check, then evaluate only each plane's positive
vertex with the **same** arithmetic and comparison as the tri-state routine:

```java
for (int i = 0; i < planeCount; ++i) {
    float[] p = planes[i];
    float x = p[0] < 0.0f ? minX : maxX;
    float y = p[1] < 0.0f ? minY : maxY;
    float z = p[2] < 0.0f ? minZ : maxZ;
    float dot = useFma
        ? Math.fma(p[0], x, Math.fma(p[1], y, p[2] * z))
        : p[0] * x + (p[1] * y + p[2] * z);
    if (!(dot >= -p[3])) return false;
}
return true;
```

This pseudocode describes the proposed pure math path, not an existing change.
Use explicitly grouped float intermediates matching `safeFMA` if a test/compiler
setting could otherwise alter the arithmetic. Do not alter plane generation,
distance limits, inputs, clipping padding or visible section lists.

Proof against the original `checkCornerVisibility(...) > 0` is direct:
the original returns zero if and only if one of those positive comparisons
fails. Its negative comparisons can only select the nonzero result 1 versus
2. Discarding them in a boolean-only consumer therefore produces the same
result for all float inputs, including unusual ones, provided positive
selection/evaluation/rejection is unchanged.

| Per surviving plane | Original FMA path | Proposed boolean path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dot work | 5 FMA calls + 1 ordinary multiply | 2 FMA calls + 1 ordinary multiply |
| Coordinate sign selections | 6 | 3 |
| Fully-inside flag/comparison | Always computed | Absent |
| Non-FMA work | 6 multiplications + 5 additions | 3 multiplications + 2 additions |

An AABB rejected by its first positive test saves little, while intersecting
or fully visible boxes save the negative work for all preceding/surviving
planes. With thirteen surviving planes this removes up to 39 FMA evaluations;
these are source operation counts, not a promised instruction/time saving.
The JIT may inline and optimize the original; measure compiled behavior.

Do **not** simply redirect to the existing `checkCornerVisibilityBool`:
that method always calls FMA and rejects with `< -pw`. A NaN positive dot
passes that rejection, whereas the tri-state acceptance `>= -pw` rejects it.
Its bytecode uses `fcmpg` for the former and `fcmpl` for the latter. They are
not exact substitutes, even if ordinary finite scene inputs usually agree.

Keep these details exact:

- Tangency (`dot == -pw`) remains visible. Preserve the original sign branch
  for both `+0.0` and `-0.0`; do not replace it with raw sign-bit selection.
- NaN coefficients/endpoints, infinities, overflow, subnormal values and
  inverted min/max endpoints retain the original evaluation behavior. Do not
  normalize/sort/clamp or add a new "conservative" NaN rule.
- Sodium inputs are already camera relative. Subtracting frustum x/y/z again
  would corrupt culling. Preserve `boxCuller.isCulledSodium` exactly.
- Reversed frusta override `testAab`: first distance-cull, then immediately
  accept a box inside their alternate box culler, otherwise classify. Keep
  that order and change only their final boolean plane-test call.

A narrow version-pinned mixin can replace only the tri-state invocation used
by `AdvancedShadowCullingFrustum.testAab` and its reversed override with a
boolean helper encoded as 0/1. Other callers retain exact 0/1/2 behavior.
Avoid a thread-local "boolean mode" or globally weakening the classifier.
Preserve disabled behavior and fail clearly if the exact target methods change.

## Verified Sodium and DH consumer paths

Pinned Sodium `render.viewport.Viewport.isBoxVisible(IIIFFF)` computes each
relative center from integer camera origin plus fractional offset, then calls
the frustum interface's `testAab` with center minus/plus extents (offsets 60–99).
`chunk.occlusion.OcclusionCuller.isWithinFrustum` supplies section centers and
**9.125f** extents. Preserve that padding; changing it is geometry culling,
not equivalent math optimization.

Iris `ReversedAdvancedShadowCullingFrustum.testAab` also ultimately uses the
tri-state classifier's boolean result, but has distinct distance/box behavior
as described above. Photon colored-light variants can select reversed culling;
the current Mac mask's disabled colored lights do not validate that branch.

Iris's DH mixin `compat.dh.mixin.MixinAdvancedShadowCullingFrustum.intersects`
builds a world-space box using the provided section x/z/width and saved world
min/max Y, calls `isVisible(DDDDDD)`, then uses nonzero. This is a separate
potential boolean consumer, but it needs original double subtraction/float
conversion and the DH interface's dimensional bounds preserved. Do not fold
it into the first Sodium-only prototype without differential tests.

## Rank 2: stop negative work after intersection is established

For tri-state consumers that genuinely need 1/2, keep every positive plane
test and the original return codes. Compute the negative expression only
while the fully-inside flag is still true. Once any negative comparison fails,
the final result can never return 1, so later negative expressions cannot
change the final result; they have no side effects. Outside rejection still
runs on all following planes and can still return 0.

This preserves finite and non-finite arithmetic outcomes used by the result;
it omits only pure expressions whose boolean conjunction is already false.
It can save up to three FMA evaluations for each subsequent surviving plane,
but adds a flag branch and does not help boxes inside all planes. Benchmark
inside/intersect/reject distributions before adopting it. This is secondary
to removing all negative work in the actual boolean Sodium consumer.

Do not change to a center/extents radius formula as the first optimization:
it introduces half-sums, absolute-value products and different rounding.
Precomputed plane sign masks are a smaller optional follow-up, but constructor
cost and JIT constant/branch behavior must justify them. The current method
already has no per-box allocations to eliminate.

## Visibility preparation is not demonstrated redundant work

`ShadowRenderer.renderShadows` prepares terrain and entity frusta separately
(bytecode calls at offsets 359 and 651), invokes terrain setup with its shadow
frustum (421), and wraps the phase with culling-state save/restore where the
LevelRenderer implements `CullingDataCache` (272 / 1064). Different frusta can
have different distance/entity settings; these calls are not interchangeable.

Pinned `compat.sodium.mixin.MixinRenderSectionManagerShadow` already keeps
separate shadow render/task lists and suppresses chunk update/upload work
inside the shadow phase. `MixinSodiumWorldRenderer` forces a shadow graph
rebuild when the interpolated sun angle changes, otherwise delegates to
`RenderSectionManager.needsUpdate`. It also terminates the shadow rebuild
loop rather than repeating the ordinary world loop. Sodium world setup
already uses graph-dirty/needs-update state.

A second world/shadow visibility pass therefore cannot be removed just
because the camera stayed still. Correct reuse needs epochs covering world
and dimension identity, renderer/pipeline reload, exact camera/frustum planes,
sun angle/light vector and shadow projection/texel snap, render/distance
settings, fog/occlusion mode, section add/remove/rebuild/upload and visibility
graph changes, plus the appropriate world versus shadow list generation.
Entities, block entities and optional DH buffers have their own lifetimes.
Until those generations are actually available and tested, cross-frame list
caching is a higher-risk unproven design, not a ranked implementation.

## Acceptance plan and stop boundary

1. Differential pure math tests compare the new boolean result to original
   tri-state `>0` for both FMA and fallback arithmetic. Generate plane sets
   and boxes with inside/intersect/outside cases, zero planes, tangency and
   adjacent ULP boundaries, negative coordinates, signed zeros, subnormals,
   huge/overflow values, infinities, NaNs and inverted endpoints. Test the
   reversed box/distance acceptance order separately. Preserve the original
   code as an independent oracle instead of mirroring the new helper.
2. Test the tri-state lazy-negative candidate against exact original 0/1/2
   results over the same cases. Test caller conversion behavior separately,
   including Sodium camera-relative values and optional DH world-space casts.
3. A warmed Java 21 microbenchmark compares baseline/helper with observable
   result checksums and realistic mixed plane/box distributions; repeat runs
   with FMA enabled/disabled. Inspect allocation and JIT inlining rather than
   assuming helper extraction saves work. This does not promise whole-frame
   speedup.
4. Runtime validation uses the original pinned Photon quality settings,
   unchanged section/shadow distances, matched camera and movement. Compare
   exact visible-section/caster identities and counts, shadows at plane edges,
   world/chunk reloads and reversed/optional-DH cases where supported. Then
   repeated serial frame/CPU timing compares feature absent/disabled/enabled,
   with and without the optional optimizer stack. GPU queries stay disabled
   for the CPU proof unless separately shown low overhead.

Stop if differential correctness fails or compiled tests/runtime show no
useful net benefit. Native multidraw and copy samples motivate other profiling,
but this pure CPU change cannot eliminate driver submission or texture-copy
work. It also cannot establish a generalized shader benefit or unlock second
shader support by itself.

# Terminal loaded-water scene survey

`WaterSceneSurvey.captureTerminalSnapshot(Minecraft client)` is an opt-in,
development-only read-only survey. It can help choose source-surveyed camera
anchors for targeted water tests. It does not establish glints, unobstructed
views, continuous water depth, shader quality, performance or safe underwater
camera placement. Compilation, actual survey execution and image/scene checks
belong to the root runtime owner. The author launched no client.

## Fixed cells, load guards and bounds

The candidate grid is exactly x `[240,300,400,500,650]`, z `[640,660,680]`,
y `[40..80]` inclusive: 15 columns and 615 candidate cells. Coordinates are
world block units; camera position is actual main-camera doubles and rotations
are degrees. No x260 column was added; x300/x400 may provide usable surveyed
alternatives, but that remains unverified until the report and scene are read.

Every world-state read first checks `client.level.hasChunkAt(pos)` **and**
`client.level.getChunkSource().hasChunk(x >> 4, z >> 4)`. This double guard is
necessary: Minecraft 1.21.1 `ClientLevel.hasChunk(int,int)` returns true
unconditionally. `ChunkSource.hasChunk` delegates to
`ClientChunkCache.getChunk(..., ChunkStatus.FULL, false)`, which returns null
for an absent/out-of-range cache entry without loading or generating terrain.
The survey never directly calls `getChunk`, requests server chunks, or uses a
heightmap. Missing chunks/out-of-build-range cells are unknown, never synthetic
AIR/water/empty terrain.

A loaded-only `BlockGetter` facade provides a cache shared by column cells,
camera context and any neighbor-dependent fluid-height/solid/collision getters.
It permits at most 4096 direct `ClientLevel.getBlockState` calls; each cached
immutable state also supplies its fluid state. All neighbor reads receive the
same double guard and budget. Block-entity-dependent context is unknown because
the facade deliberately declines that lookup. A known basic block/fluid record
remains known if a contextual shape/height field becomes unknown. The report
exposes actual direct read and unique cached-position counts, and budget status.
Biome sampling is omitted to avoid hidden neighboring lookups.

Actual `Camera.getFluidInCamera()` is called at most once. The exact cached
source reads the eye cell, up to five near-plane cells, and water/lava height
checks may read the cell above each. Before calling it, the survey guards and
preloads all six possible cells plus their above cells: at most 12 unique
positions. Its internal repeated block/fluid lookups are not instrumented;
17 is a conservative source-derived upper bound. The total world-state getter
call ceiling is therefore 4096 direct facade misses +17 camera-internal reads
=4113, not a silently claimed 615 total reads. All possible camera lookup
positions have been preloaded into the same bounded cache first. No FogType
query runs if its positions are missing/unavailable or the camera is not
initialized in the current camera-entity client level.
The camera-internal bound applies to the inspected Minecraft Camera method and
vanilla water/lava height implementations in the pinned development stack;
mods replacing those implementations require a fresh audit.

## Fields and interpretation

The terminal JSON records dimension, game/day time, day-time modulo 24000,
sky-light/ceiling flags, rain/thunder values at interpolation partial tick zero,
and current rain/thunder booleans. These are world inputs, not shader wetness
supplier reevaluations or a sun-glint forecast. Main-camera position/rotation,
initialized/detached state, configured camera type/first-person flag, actual
FogType, and its loaded cell's block/fluid/solid/collision flags are included.
The camera's `detached` flag and configured camera type are separately reported;
player feet coordinates are not substituted for the eye position.

Each sampled cell records registry block/fluid names, AIR, can-occlude, fluid
empty/water/source/amount, fluid height, solid-render and empty-collision-shape
flags. A waterlogged collision block may have water and nonempty collision
together; water does not imply safe camera placement. Each column records
observed water/nonempty-fluid counts, range completeness and the greatest
observed water-cell top in y40..80 when a height is known. That bounded maximum
is not proof of the entire column's surface or a measured continuous depth.
Missing cells and failed contexts remain explicit unknown objects.

Tentative west-facing glint anchor `(400.5,68,680.5)` and older x240 shoreline
remain proposals. The survey reads integer cell `(400,y,680)` but does not move
the camera, set yaw/time/weather or validate those proposals. Root must inspect
loaded-water continuity/collision and actual near/far/glint/underwater captures
before adopting camera anchors or making quality claims.

## Scene recovery source context

The exact lease implementation is [SceneLease](../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/SceneLease.java:45), not BenchmarkWorld. `prepare` permits only a private singleplayer server with one player. `freeze` captures its prior frozen state in the submitted server task before freezing. `close` sets cancellation, submits restoration of that captured state on the same server, then waits up to two seconds on the task future; it marks the lease closed only after that future completes normally. Timeout or exceptional completion throws and leaves ownership retained; retry reuses an unfinished restoration future or replaces an exceptionally completed one. This is an actual server-task completion barrier in the source, not a fire-and-forget request.

[AutoTuner.restoreOwnedState](../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/AutoTuner.java:498) first requires the exact original source/current family, restores core/preset through public Apply, restores the original independent flags through the guarded edit transaction, and restores video. It then closes the lease, nulls the lease only after successful close, and writes `RESTORED` through the journal. [restore](../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/AutoTuner.java:478) clears the Job only when that whole recovery operation returns COMPLETE. A failed close keeps its lease reference and throws; retries park after three failures with PENDING recovery and the Job retained. Normal terminal [finish](../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/AutoTuner.java:437) also closes the lease before journal completion and Job release.

[TuningJournal](../../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/TuningJournal.java:15) writes the original `PENDING` Undo state atomically before `Job.start` prepares/freezes the scene. Both retained `undo-original.properties` files contain `state=PENDING`; the cancelled run metadata contains `result=RESTORED`, and the later status is inactive and world-ready. These retained runtime artifacts, combined with the compiled implementation ordering above, support successful source-context recovery through the server-task completion barrier. The prior paragraph's telemetry caveat means **no separately captured physical simulation-tick snapshot or explicit acknowledgement event**, not an absent acknowledgement barrier in the implementation. We did not directly measure resumed tick advancement or independently read back the server frozen state after close. The naturally INCOMPLETE second run uses the same close-before-terminal ordering. No new runtime action or test was performed for this clarification; commands are released.

Photon atmosphere units and its shifted planet origin stay upstream. The radial
entry position in camera-relative blocks is explicitly
`direction * (dists.x / CLOUDS_SCALE)`, and distance is its Euclidean length.
The viewer's atmosphere origin shift is subtracted analytically by using the ray

# Benchmark guide

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

G01 MakeUp copy elimination and G02 BSL mip elimination also collect existing untimed work witnesses after each measurement, disarming them before further timing. The BSL witness requires a separate untimed reload; inspect its completeness rather than inferring execution from parsed directives. G04 MakeUp `translucent_fastpath` requires `--saved-pose 9`: the maintained caller places one honey block in the backed-up save before all arms to cover the non-water/glass translucent class. Client visibility is checked; whole-save restoration removes the fixture after shutdown, including failed runs. Use `--width` and `--height` for the actual fullscreen mode (currently 2560×1600 on the local Asahi display).

The standard test records the prepared profile’s resource-pack file identities and freezes its selection requests. It requires those requests to be loaded before conditioning and checks the same actual selection before every arm; silent incompatible-pack removal refuses timing. Selection is enforced at those boundaries; resource bytes are not continuously rehashed. Saved pose11 is a close view of the existing stone gallery for native PBR material coverage.

G03 MakeUp early-alpha captures existing qualified-draw counters in snapshots and its untimed source/admission diagnostic after each arm. The permission-based route requires an admitted context beforehand and qualified-counter progress afterward; these are admission counts, not avoided fragments. The Asahi post-sample route has no draw permission: it instead requires the typed rewrite receipt and all current source/input checks. Its timing remains explicitly source-setup-only evidence, without linked consumption or fragment coverage proof. CPU-cost profiling remains disabled for ordinary plans.

BSL reflection and AO sample-reuse tests retain untimed draw-admission status; admission is not a saved-query count. Photon is validated by its separate pinned live-pixel-budget producer and manifest. Its generated solid-terrain program marker is checked at its exact declared value; unknown added options and changes to original native options still fail.

The standard test also accepts `--candidate c01-bounds` without `--feature` for the existing finite private extra-occlusion prototype. It requires the exact original MakeUp9.5g/native100 map and no DH. Both controls and the candidate retain master Off with empty public requests; only the private current-frame query mode changes (prefix1, groups32). Actual query/read progress is required before and after candidate timing. This is separate from public depth priming.

Use `--candidate g10-exact-bloom` without `--feature` for the finite private MakeUp exact zero-dither bloom reuse variant. It preserves native100 and four original additions, and requires an actual pre-detach compile/link receipt joined to consuming bloom draws. The original pack is used for both Off controls. Staged private packs and sidecars are backed up/restored by the operation; diagnostic reloads acknowledge rendered readiness and settled configuration. An integer work image runs after all three timed arms, with its actual writer texture joined to readback. Source-expression opportunity counts are not hardware-fetch savings. `--candidate g10-native-control` uses the same private producer with selector0 and requires native linked source; it is explicitly labeled a known-null control, with descriptive timing retained and no optimization conclusion.

The experimental combination command accepts `--features dead_frame_copy,early_alpha,translucent_fastpath,ao_attenuation` instead of `--feature`, with any supported subset of two to four MakeUp G01/G03/G04/G06 features. It enables explicit benchmark-only admission and preserves the native100/API/platform/source checks. Every requested compile control must be active. G01 requires complete executed-copy witnesses (6/3/6 per completed final pass), including candidate coverage before timing; G04 and G06 require matching selected-source markers. G03 retains its complete native CUTOUT fragment pin and obtains untimed shader-object/link/submission evidence; submitted batches are not avoided-fragment counts. Witnesses disarm in `finally`, and timing refuses an armed G03 observer. Ordinary clients retain their prior route restrictions. This measures tested subsets; it does not establish an exhaustive optimum or an all-twelve-active configuration.

`--scene translucent-fixture --saved-pose 9` uses the maintained honey-block fixture for every arm, including subsets without G04. G04 uses that fixture by default. `--scene saved` explicitly retains the unmodified authored saved scene, allowing coverage and performance scenes to be considered separately; record its saved pose and do not infer G04 branch coverage from the request flag. Whole-save/profile restoration remains mandatory.

`--with-g10` adds the private exact zero-dither G10 kernel to an explicit supported combination. `--g10-control` uses the same observer setup with the kernel disabled. Both collect completed draws in explicit untimed intervals and refuse timing if the observer remains armed. The pre/post draw counters describe those untimed intervals, not timed work. A qualified constructor gate is separate from native options; approximate pairing is never enabled. The observer must join actual compiled shader objects, successful link and consuming draws at the actual bloom stage (composite2 when G01 moves it). Missing link/source/progress evidence refuses timing. `--candidate c01-bounds --features ...` similarly tests the finite private C01 addition with generated-source/native100 verification, unchanged attached native SOLID hashes and existing query/depth/raster checks. These additions are development experiments; original-only C01/G10 commands remain available. Physical fetch savings, motion/pixel equivalence and broad DH/PBR compatibility require separate evidence.

If the harness or inputs fail, preserve the failure, restore/release owned resources, fix the maintained harness or inputs, and retry. Do not copy harness code into report-local callers, inject launcher overrides, relax admission after failure, or substitute custom scripts for the standard result. Diagnostics are diagnostic and do not replace it. One Linux ARM64 BSL standard run completed with verified restoration and independent review; this does not establish behavior for other configurations or future changes. See [experiment history](EXPERIMENTS.md).

Keep reports, worlds, downloads, builds and captures out of Git. Do not kill unrelated processes. If restoration refuses due to unknown changes, preserve the data and inspect ownership and recovery before acting.

Runtime dependencies and original shader-pack inputs are stored under `dependencies/`. Keep active experiment output in `dev/experiments/` and any retained evidence in `experiment-evidence/`; both are local and outside Git. Prepared clients and worlds remain under `run-workloads/`.

# Agent operations

## Goals and teams

The native Codex Goal sustains work in a chat. `docs/STATUS.md` and its linked
`docs/goals/` checkpoint preserve the project between sessions. The user requests
new goals; the repository-local `$start-goal-team` skill supports that workflow.
Do not silently replace an unfinished goal or create a new user-owned chat.

Use native subagents for independent subtasks. Assign deliverables, files,
acceptance evidence, and stopping boundaries before launch. The project has
four optional profiles under `.codex/agents/`: `feature_owner`, `shader_owner`,
`runtime_operator`, and `research_advisor`. They inherit the parent model and
reasoning settings. Roles are responsibilities, not a required team size.

For initial setup, explicit file partitions in a shared checkout are practical.
For overlapping or larger edits, use isolated worktrees and integrate only
reviewed work. A worker reports findings to the orchestrator; the orchestrator
owns the final checkpoint and speaks to the user.

## Client and GPU ownership

One agent owns the interactive Minecraft client, shader reloads, world changes,
and GPU capture at a time. Record the run command, process/session identifier,
run directory, active shader pack, scene, and how to stop the owned process.
Before handing off, verify whether the client is still running. Do not stop
unrelated Java or game processes by broad process-name matching.

Build success establishes Java/build integration. A title screen establishes
startup. In-world rendering establishes shader compilation and scene behavior.
DH presence in a mod list does not establish DH terrain rendering. Use
`docs/EVALUATION.md` to keep these evidence levels distinct.

No remote GPU host is configured by this scaffold. If later authorized, record
hardware and connection procedures explicitly rather than copying another
project's host identities. A local Mac result does not validate Windows/Linux
GPU behavior.

## Checkpoints and handoffs

Update the active goal at milestones with completed work, exact checks and
results, selected dependency revisions, relevant commits, active agents,
worktrees, owned processes, unresolved decisions, and the next action. Keep
full logs and captures in ignored runtime/output directories and link them from
the checkpoint when needed.

The `SessionStart` hook emits a checkpoint reminder on startup, resume, and
compaction. It does not launch replacement chats, impose a context limit, or
transfer process ownership. After compaction, re-read the checkpoint and verify
live jobs; when a handoff is useful, finish or explicitly transfer live work
within the user's authorized scope. Durable files remain useful if hooks are
unavailable or their repository trust has not been enabled.

## Git and external actions

Do not copy sibling Git history, remotes, project identities, or user secrets.
Keep commits coherent and subjects short, with no coauthor trailers. Publishing,
remote pushes, and messages to external services require authorization from the
user's request; local agent instructions do not grant it. Preserve unmerged
work before removing any worktree. Avoid broad `git clean` in the shared checkout.

Downloaded jars, launch directories, shader source checkouts, world saves,
screenshots, GPU captures, and raw logs stay out of Git. Record versions/hashes
and keep local reproduction scripts plus maintained patches in Git. Preserve
upstream licenses and source ancestry for shader derivatives.

Configuration follows the official [subagent documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents)
and [hook documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks). The repository
skill follows the [skills workflow](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills).

# Exact shadow visibility traversal source gate R1

2026-10-07. Read-only gate for Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.253 /
Iris 1.8.12 / Sodium 0.6.13. Parent owns integration, checkpoints and the idle
client/GPU. This worker changed only this report and ignored

## Decision

**Exact CPU shadow-terrain traversal reuse is neither implemented nor enabled.
Reject an immediate traversal-skipping pilot on the current contracts.** Accept
the specific source seam as technically plausible: replace only the body of
`RenderSectionManager.createTerrainRenderList(Camera, Viewport, int, boolean)`
on a fully certified exact hit, replay its mutable visibility/list side effects,
and let all native terrain/entity/block-entity draws and current uniforms proceed.
The existing code does not yet supply that certificate or replay.

The missing work is concrete rather than a GPU map-cache problem: complete
structural/task producer generations, exact prepared traversal inputs, isolated
inner-list ownership on the actual pack, touched-section write provenance,
generation retagging, and safe current task maps. A camera/sun comparison plus an
old outer list cannot satisfy it. Current evidence earns this source decision,
not implementation authorization, a performance prediction or a new framework.

R11 is a degraded **joint-family** diagnostic: native 163 / 158 FPS, removal
199 / 177, return 139 / 145. Actual point states, native options and visible
removal/restoration were verified by the parent; control variation limits an
exact cost claim. It does not identify traversal CPU time, critical-path overlap,
isolated shadow-generation cost or a quality-preserving product gain. No 20%
prediction follows.

## Actual callsite and list lifecycle

1. `ShadowRenderer.renderShadows` constructs/prepares its terrain frustum,
   temporarily sets `Minecraft.smartCull=false` at bytecode 384, calls
   `LevelRenderer.needsUpdate()` at 399, then `invokeSetupRender(..., false,
   false)` at 421; smartCull restoration is at 429. Sodium's LevelRenderer mixin
   routes the explicit update into `SodiumWorldRenderer.scheduleTerrainUpdate`
   and `RenderSectionManager.markGraphDirty`.
2. `SodiumWorldRenderer.setupTerrain` still processes chunk events, radius reload,
   camera/projection/fog dirtiness, camera state and translucent movement triggers.
   Its ordinary clean-graph optimization exists already. The unconditional Iris
   shadow mark defeats a clean shadow hit; its sun-angle redirect cannot undo it.
3. Manager `update` increments `lastUpdatedFrame` at bytecode 0–7 and invokes
   `createTerrainRenderList` at 18. Iris `cancelIfShadow` injects **AFTER this
   invocation** and cancels before the normal dirty clear at 23. Shadow traversal
   has already run; the main traversal deliberately remains dirty. A cancellation
   at update/setup HEAD loses original generation and setup side effects.
4. `createTerrainRenderList` resets lists at 1, obtains effective search/mode,
   constructs `VisibleChunkCollector`, calls `OcclusionCuller.findVisible` at 41,
   sorts/installs outer lists at 48–51 and installs rebuild maps at 57–60. These
   are the exact replacement obligations. Keep update's call boundary, dirty
   mark and Iris after-call cancellation intact.
5. Iris redirects creation/reset/selected draw and task field accesses to
   `shadowRenderLists` / `shadowTaskLists`. It cancels shadow `updateChunks` and
   `uploadChunks` at HEAD and stops the loop after one shadow iteration. Native
   setup cleanup/sprite work outside these cancellations must continue.
6. `RenderRegion.getRenderList()` otherwise returns one persistent owner-local
   `ChunkRenderList`; collector resets/adds/sorts that object. `SortedRenderLists`
   stores references, not immutable copies. Main subsequently overwrites the
   inner arrays unless the mod's optional separation is active.

The current mod has only `ShadowRegionListsMixin.getRenderList` selection and
`ShadowSpriteListsMixin`'s generation-aware sprite adapter. Its controller says
it does not authorize traversal reuse. `separateShadowVisibilityLists` defaults
false and activation additionally requires global enabled, an in-world usable
Photon pack named exactly `Photon-ShaderLOD.zip` or `photon_v1.3b.zip`, and no Iris
fallback. R11 uses original Complementary with global Off; its supplied config
has `enabled=false`. Therefore R11 cannot establish the optional isolated-list
prerequisite. Turning that Photon-only feature on for Complementary would itself
need actual equivalence evidence. Frustum coherence/math helpers only change
individual boolean tests; they do not skip `findVisible`.

## Required exact input contract

The actual acceptance algorithm, not a snapped camera cell, defines the key:

| Input | Exact consuming path / requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Manager/world/renderer identity | Manager owns sections, regions, culler, builder and sort state; drop snapshots on construct/destroy/reload/world replacement |
| Current prepared frustum | Supported actual frustum class, all active plane coefficient bits/count/FMA policy, primary/reversed distance constraints, prepared x/y/z, effective branch semantics; unknown classes/values miss |
| Viewport coordinates | `Viewport.isBoxVisible` subtracts actual `CameraTransform.int*` and `frac*`; graph angle tests also use full double x/y/z; include section origin and current transform values |
| Search and traversal mode | Actual `getSearchDistance()` result and `shouldUseOcclusionCulling()` result; original cylindrical strict comparisons, world min/max section, origin/nearby paths and outward direction masks |
| Sort origin/order | Collector sorts region Manhattan distance then `ChunkRenderList.sortSections` uses camera section relative to region; preserve exact outer and inner ordered membership |
| Pack/pipeline/resources/DH selection | Effective shadow range, supported pipeline and vertex-layout/resource identity, selected vanilla/DH projection/readiness; invalidate on replacement/change, keep DH's separate terrain lifecycle intact |
| Structural/task producers | Covered monotonic generations and proof of eligible empty pending/in-flight state, not the shared dirty boolean |

`CameraTransform.integral(double)` is a Java int cast (truncation), and its float
fractional calculation applies the signed 128 rounding trick. Recomputing these
from floor/cell coordinates is not the original test. Compare the actual stored
transform and exact prepared inputs; hash equality alone is insufficient.

Fresh mapped `LevelTimeAccess.getTimeOfDay(float)` bytecode ignores its parameter
and calls `DimensionType.timeOfDay(dayTime())`. The earlier corrected intra-tick
standing-camera opportunity therefore remains plausible with daylight running.
It is not measured eligibility: camera interpolation, FOV/bob/hooks or selected
DH matrices can change between frames. Current observers do not establish an
exact equal-key hit fraction.

Changing shader animation clocks, texture animation or entity poses does not
automatically invalidate **terrain graph membership** when all its actual CPU
inputs/producers are unchanged. Full native rendering still samples their current
uniforms/materials and animated poses each frame. Changes to section flags,
connectivity, bounds/producers, sprites/entities membership or renderer state do
invalidate. Do not import a whole-map content-equality gate or freeze animation
to make this CPU proposal pass.

## Producer, queue and replay obligations absent today

| Actual writer / lifecycle | Required guard or replay |
| --- | --- |
| `onSectionAdded`, `onSectionRemoved`, neighbor connections, `RenderSection.delete` | Immediate structural/lifetime/task invalidation; no disposed section/region references |
| `markGraphDirty`, direct `needsGraphUpdate=true`, camera/explicit terrain updates | Classify only the exact repeated Iris force as nonstructural; preserve its write and main rebuild. All unknown marks miss |
| `scheduleRebuild` pending promotion and section-cache invalidate | Task generation, conservative structural miss until resulting info is accounted for |
| `processChunkBuildResults` / `updateSectionInfo` | Upload normal native storage; cover built/flags/visibility/global-entity changes and task token retirement/upload stamp; unchanged membership never licenses cached draw offsets |
| `processGFNIMovement`, `scheduleSort`, `prepareTrigger`, translucent data integration | Separate sort/task generation; `scheduleSort` can change pending state without any graph-dirty write |
| `submitSectionTasks`, cancellation tokens, lastSubmitted/lastUpload, result queue and collectors | Do not resurrect old queued tasks, lose fresh jobs or infer task safety from graph cleanliness. First design must miss on relevant pending/active/unknown work |
| Region `cleanupAndFlip`, native storage upload/arena relocation | Continue existing APIs; own only membership arrays, never native draw pointers/storage offsets |
| Culler `visitNode`, origin and nearby paths | Replay current traversal stamp for every touched section, including rejected/enqueued/empty nodes; replay only direction writes the original traversal performed |
| Collector lists and sprite/entity consumers | Retag current generation without clearing cached arrays; restore current shadow outer list and proven-current empty task maps; retain exact ordered geometry/sprite/entity membership and native consumer behavior |
| Frame counter wrap and toggles/fallback/reload | Drop cache before ambiguous generation reuse, reset on identity/eligibility change, fall back immediately |

One precision correction to the older design: `OcclusionCuller.addNearbySections`
stamps a newly added nearby section but **does not reset incomingDirections**
(source 250–254; bytecode stamp at 121). `visitNode` resets/unions directions and
`initWithinWorld` resets origin directions. A replay of cached final direction
values for every touched section would overwrite state the nearby-only original
path leaves untouched after an intervening main traversal. Capture the direction
write mask/provenance and replay those writes only. A rendered-section snapshot
cannot recover that distinction, nor the queued sections rejected before visit.

There is no current mixin covering these producer generations or touched writes,
no immutable complete traversal snapshot, and no list generation-only retag API.
`ChunkRenderList.reset(int)` clears counts and size as well as setting its stamp;
using it on a hit destroys membership. Main graph metadata is shared across
phases even when inner arrays are isolated, so replay is at least O(touched
sections), not constant-time pointer reuse.

The existing phase observer reads actual Iris shadow outer lists through bounded
reflection and captures selected region memberships around shadow/main phases.
It is a no-skip ownership diagnostic, not complete per-traversal input, task,
stamp/direction-write or invalidation coverage. ShadowInputObserver is likewise
not a terrain-producer certificate. Its map-reuse zero does not reject this CPU
idea; its clock/caster summaries do not prove it safe either.

## Bounded acceptance and stopping boundary

A future single pinned exact-cache implementation could be quality-preserving
only after its no-skip snapshots demonstrate complete guards and replay against
the always-traverse path. Required differential evidence includes exact ordered
lists, all touched-section stamp/direction writes, sprite activation/native
entity visibility, preserved main dirtying, empty/pending task treatment, edits,
async completion/sorts, loading/unloading, day ticks/camera/FOV, toggles and
world/pack/resource/DH changes. All original shadow draws, clears, matrices,
current uniforms, animated casters, composites and target work must remain.
Unknown producers/classes or incomplete snapshots take the original traversal.

Only after that correctness gate could a serial matched measurement establish
traversal/replay cost and total rendering benefit in normal standing, turning,
walking/loading gameplay. R11 provides neither cost attribution nor a reason to
skip this contract. No GPU shadow-map reuse, cadence, caster dropping, quality
setting change, envelope/epsilon approximation or modern-port rollout is earned.

This exact 1.21.1 contract is not automatically applicable to 1.21.11, 26.1.2,
26.2, 26.3, another Iris/Sodium pair or Fabric. This gate did not inspect those
binaries; class signatures, mixin ordering, queue/lifecycle and frustum behavior
must be re-established per pair. Current Photon-only hook eligibility also does
not establish general-pack compatibility.

Stop here: **no skip implementation or new runtime lane is source-ready on the
current evidence.** The parent may select completion of this narrowly identified
CPU contract as separate bounded work, or reject its priority in favor of the
independent shader-source gate. This worker owns no live jobs or client state.

# Optional-stack forest results

2026-10-05. Nine serial original-Photon captures completed in exec session34175
(exit0). No meaningful consistent stack gain was established. ShaderLOD's main
mod was absent from every arm; these are optional-stack results, not shader LOD
performance. No optimizer default or recommended stack changes follow.

Minecraft1.21.1 / NeoForge21.1.253 / Iris1.8.12 / Sodium0.6.13 / Photonv1.3b /
DH3.3.3, Apple M3Max / OpenGL4.1 Metal91.7. Locks retain exact artifact hashes.
Forest camera256.5/95/768.5 yaw135 pitch9, clear time7000, detailed24 / DH128,
1488×836 framebuffer. Every run:45s warmup,25s capture, fixed shaderwetness0,
frame-only asynchronous elapsed query one frame in16; CPU layers off. Actual
effective options, world/camera/radii and sampled window/pacing state match.
All observed capture windows focused/visible, unminimized, uncapped260/Vsyncfalse.

## Median independent-run observations

Each row is three JVM launches, not three frame samples. GPU values are medians
of each capture's mean elapsed game-render interval, not inverse FPS.

| Stack | FPS range | Frame median ms | GPU median-of-means ms | Thread median ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| minimal | 120.25–121.20 | 8.277 | 7.765 | 7.462 |
| optimized | 109.36–124.21 | 8.183 | 7.635 | 7.391 |
| optimized-culling | 104.55–122.31 | 8.407 | 7.746 | 7.413 |

## Paired block reductions

Positive is faster. Partial Williams cycle: order is interleaved, not fully
position-balanced. Frame reductions change sign; no confidence/significance
claim is supported by three correlated-host blocks.

| Baseline → candidate | Frame reductions by block | GPU mean reductions by block |
| --- | --- | --- |
| minimal → optimized | +3.18%, -10.48%, +0.83% | +6.03%, -9.20%, +1.68% |
| minimal → optimized-culling | -15.02%, -1.57%, +0.91% | -11.83%, -0.39%, +1.50% |
| optimized → optimized-culling | -18.80%, +8.07%, +0.08% | -19.00%, +8.06%, -0.18% |

## Artifact qualification and scope

Strict raw-archive comparison rejects the varying embedded fabric_api_base
identity. The qualified analysis explicitly accepts only the audited exact pair
on this pinned runtime:17 identical class files and identical resources except
a satisfied NeoForge minimum-version dependency bound. Raw identities and
provider variants remain in every report/comparison. This is a qualified
comparison, not byte-identical whole runtime or deterministic provider selection.
See CULLING_EMBEDDED_PROVENANCE.md and dev/runtime-artifact-equivalences.json.

All optional parent versions/hashes loaded correctly, including EntityCulling
1.11.2, TRansition1.0.25 and TRender1.0.17. Root inspected baseline/culling PNGs:
no gross terrain/cloud/shadow loss in the fixed forest; DH VBOs rendered. This
does not validate entity-rich occlusion, out-of-bounds block entities, moving
shadow casters or shader UI. Sheep/world simulation and animation clocks
advance; positions are not frozen. Culling is not aimed at this terrain-heavy
scene and no general culling benefit is inferred.

Development class directories were not byte-fingerprinted by these reports.
Loaded jars are hashed; dev source did not change during the matrix, but raw
reports do not independently prove class-directory byte identity. After the
matrix, the overlay was updated for pack-neutral labels; future captures must
not be pooled with these solely from the unchanged dev version string.

Raw retained evidence: dev/logs/takeover-stack-forest-r1, runner console next
to it. The failed strict-analysis log remains alongside successful qualified
stack-analysis-qualified.json. All screenshots/UUIDs/failures are retained.
Next: entity-rich compatibility if pursuing culling, plus matched shader
experiments under a held-constant stack. Ordinary Photon≥15%/second-workload
performance gate remains unmet.
